lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Hi Phillip. Dim2 aa3? Hi Phillip. How’s it going?

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Long time no see! Where did you spend your Christmas? Did you do anything fun?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Christmas...I stayed in Hong Kong for Christmas. But...uh no wait, I went to Korea! Hahaha...

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: You went to Korea? Hey that’s really nice, going to Korea.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes, I went with...

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: I’ve been there once.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I went to Korea with my mom. Since she’s been obsessing over a celebrity called Park Bo-gum recently, I tagged along with her to Korea to see stuff about him. So...yeah, Korea is pretty nice. I mean the food there, and the culture, it’s all...pretty nice.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Isn’t it really cold to go to Korea now?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: It’s cold, really cold.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: It should be snowing, right?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Er...it so happened that when I was there, it wasn’t snowing at all. Uh...we got a thin layer of snow one morning, but it was gone quite soon.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: I’ve been to Korea once too, but the food there wasn’t particularly good, I mean you eat chicken uh...you eat pork and chicken and so on.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes, things like that.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Yup. The food was pretty average. Like kimchi...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: But...I guess I’m personally rather...uh keen on eating. So I found it...delicious. Like the samgye-tang (ginseng chicken) or...the tteok-bokki (Korean rice cake) and so on. The street food was all really tasty. So...

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Well I was initially planning a trip to Taiwan this Christmas. But since it was the holiday season, you know the flights got quite expensive, so in the end I went to the mainland.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: So where did you go on the mainland?

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Where on the mainland? I joined one of those two-day package tours, which brought us to Shunde to...go to amusement parks, things like that. Uh...I travelled to the mainland mainly just because it was cheap.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: That’s true. There it’s like...I can’t tell haha.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: But I’m going to Taiwan in April.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Oh in April...where are you going in Taiwan? Tai...pei?

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: I like to go to Taiwan a lot, after all I’ve been there two...times already. The first time I went to Taipei, and the second time to Taichung, uh Alishan...oops sorry, Taichung should be around...where the Sun Moon Lake is. Whereas this time I’m planning to go to Alishan.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Aww I’d love to go to Alishan too! I was planning to go with Karen a while ago, but unfortunately I couldn’t take leave from my work, and...I couldn’t go with her. Anyway I do hope I have another chance to go there someday.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Oh right.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Anyway...do you like Taipei? The food is rather cheap there.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Taipei isn’t exactly my favourite, I mean in Taipei it feels like being back in Hong Kong.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Oh...it kind of does...

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: So I prefer the rural (mountainous) areas in Taichung...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Taichung uh...well I....

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: where I can really unwind...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: well I’ve never been to Taichung myself, so I’d like to...check it out too. When I do, I can ask you for an overview now.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: I can get you some photos.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes, please do. I’ll get you to suggest places for me to go.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: For sure. You seem to like travelling a lot in general.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: In general...I like it because sometimes it’s...for one I grew up abroad and got used to it, I guess, and when I’m in Hong Kong, where it’s so cramped everywhere, sometimes I do want to explore other places, so I often...maybe try to spend less, so that I can save up some money for travelling, to be exposed to other places, to see different things, and most importantly to...eat. Because...I really like...eating lots of different things.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Eating here and there.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes, eating here and there.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Then you’d love Taiwan for sure. Delicacies everywhere.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yep, Taiwan is great too. So much good food. Maybe someday...we could go together in April.

lines.speaker: Phillip
lines.english: Yes, great idea! Okay。 Okay. Okay.

definition_overrides.tung4__同: None of the listed senses (diarrhoea, lane, alley) actually fit here — in this sentence 同 is being used as a preposition meaning "with" (as in "went with [someone]"), which isn't one of the given senses.
definition_overrides.zo2__咗: Cantonese particle indicating perfective aspect for a completed action or past event.
definition_overrides.sai2__洗: to clear (as in spending/using up money)
